title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: A hedge is a row of closely planted bushes or trees that grows tall and thick, often used to surround a garden or yard.
example: For example, many homes have a hedge around their yard to keep people from seeing inside.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: A thing that stops you from doing something or getting somewhere.
example: For example, a tall fence can be a barrier between two yards.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: A place where people go to drink and relax, often with music and friends.
example: For example, a group of friends might go to a place where they can have drinks and talk.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: The study of the inside parts of living things, especially humans.
example: For example, students learn about the heart, lungs, and brain in their class on the inside of the body.

meaning: n. 流行病；(坏事的)盛行 adj. 流行性的；极为盛行的
title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: A big spread of a bad thing, like a sickness that affects many people at the same time.
example: For example, a bad cough that spreads quickly in a school is called a big spread of sickness.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: A part of a living thing that carries instructions for its body to grow and work properly.
example: For example, your eye color is decided by parts of your body that you get from your parents.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: A tiny living thing that can make people sick if it gets inside the body.
example: For example, if you don't wash your hands, you might get a cold from touching a door handle with germs on it.

meaning: n. [bacterium 的复数形式 ] 细菌
title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: Tiny living things that can be found everywhere, like in water, soil, and even inside your body. Some of them can make you sick, but others are helpful.
example: For example, when you eat spoiled food, harmful tiny living things can grow in it and make you feel sick.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: A tiny germ that can make people sick and spread easily from one person to another.
example: For example, when someone with a cold sneezes, it can spread to others through the air.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: A tiny living thing that can only be seen with a special tool called a microscope.
example: For example, bacteria in the soil are tiny living things that help break down dead plants.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: The process your body uses to turn food into energy and keep your body working properly.
example: For example, when you eat a banana, your body breaks it down and uses the energy to help you run and play.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: A type of important food that helps your body grow and stay strong.
example: For example, eggs and meat are good sources of this kind of food.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: A special kind of food that helps your body stay healthy and work properly.
example: For example, eating oranges gives your body something it needs to fight sickness.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: To make and release a substance inside the body, usually without using a tube or opening.
example: For example, the body makes sweat through the skin when it gets hot.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: To get rid of something the body doesn't need, like waste or extra water.
example: For example, when you urinate, your body is getting rid of extra water and waste.

meaning: v. 吞食，狼吞虎咽地吃
title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: To eat something very quickly and with a lot of hunger.
example: For example, the hungry dog ate his food in seconds because he was so hungry.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: It is a natural feeling or ability that helps you know something without learning it first.
example: For example, when you touch something hot, you pull your hand away without thinking.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: Something that feels easy to understand without needing to be taught or explained.
example: For example, a child might feel intuitive about how to ride a bike because it just feels natural.

meaning: n. 潜力 adj. 潜在的
title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: Something that someone or something might be able to do in the future.
example: For example, a young athlete has the potential to become a great player if they practice hard.

meaning: n. 智慧，智力；情报，谍报
title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: Intelligence is the ability to learn, understand, and think clearly. It can also mean secret information about others.
example: For example, a smart person has high intelligence, and spies collect intelligence to help their country.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: Something that works properly or has a special purpose.
example: For example, a working light is functional because it can shine bright when you turn it on.

meaning: adj. 灵敏的；过敏的；易担忧的；(话题等)须谨慎对待的
title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: Something that reacts easily to changes or feels things strongly. It can also mean something that needs to be handled carefully.
example: For example, some people have sensitive skin and get red easily when they use the wrong soap.

meaning: adj. 可弯曲的；灵活的，易变通的
title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: Something that is flexible can bend easily or change how it works. It can also mean someone who is open to new ideas or changes.
example: For example, a flexible person can change their plan when something unexpected happens.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: Something that relates to how sounds are heard or made by the ears.
example: For example, an acoustic guitar makes sound through the vibrations of its strings and body.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: Something that relates to sight or the way light works
example: For example, glasses help people see more clearly by changing how light enters their eyes.

meaning: adj. 夜间发生的；夜间活动的
title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: Something that happens or is active during the night.
example: For example, some animals like owls are awake and hunt when it is dark outside.

meaning: adj. 睡着的；休眠的；(动物等)冬眠的
title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: Something that is not active or awake, but can become active again later.
example: For example, a seed is dormant in the ground during winter and starts to grow when it gets warm.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: It is a way some animals sleep through the cold winter months to save energy.
example: For example, a bear sleeps in its cave all winter and wakes up when it gets warm again.

meaning: v. 追踪 n. 足迹，踪迹；轨道
title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: To follow something or someone closely, or the path that something leaves behind.
example: For example, a dog might follow the path of a rabbit in the snow.

meaning: v. 追踪；查出；追溯 n. 痕迹；少许
title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: To follow something or someone to find out where they went or what happened.
example: For example, the police tried to follow the thief's path to find where he was hiding.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: To take turns doing something or happening one after the other.
example: For example, you and your friend might take turns riding a bike.

meaning: n. 被捕食的动物，猎物 v. 捕食
title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: A creature that is hunted and eaten by another animal.
example: For example, a rabbit is the food of a fox.

meaning: n. 掠夺者；捕食性动物
title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: A creature that hunts and eats other animals for food.
example: For example, a lion is a creature that hunts and eats smaller animals like zebras.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: A person who is hurt or harmed by something bad that happens.
example: For example, a person who was stolen from is a person who was harmed by a thief.

meaning: n. 俘虏 adj. 被关押的；受控制的
title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: Someone who is held by another person and cannot go free. Also describes something that is controlled by someone else.
example: For example, a soldier who is taken prisoner during a war is called a captive.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: Something that is used to protect yourself or your team from being attacked or hurt.
example: For example, a player in a soccer game might act defensive by trying to stop the other team from scoring.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: To undergo means to experience something, especially something difficult or challenging.
example: For example, a patient might undergo surgery to get better.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: To suffer means to experience something bad or painful, like pain, sadness, or a problem.
example: For example, if you fall and hurt your leg, you are suffering from the pain.

meaning: adj. 易受伤的，脆弱的；易受影响的
title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: Something that is vulnerable can be easily hurt or damaged, either physically or emotionally.
example: For example, a small plant can be vulnerable to strong winds and might get broken easily.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: It means living with just enough to stay alive, but not having much extra.
example: For example, some people in poor areas get food and shelter by working very hard each day.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: To be alive or to be in a place or situation.
example: For example, trees exist in the forest and help animals live there.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: To completely destroy something so that there is none left.
example: For example, a farmer might kill all the insects in his garden to protect his plants.

meaning: v. 驯养；制服 adj. 驯服的；乏味的
title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: To make an animal or a person follow your rules, or to make something less strong.
example: For example, people can train a wild horse to live in a stable and do what they are told.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: A person who takes care of animals or watches over a place.
example: For example, the person who feeds the animals at the zoo is called a keeper.

title: Chapter 3 动物保护
english_meaning: A person who takes care of sheep and leads them to places to eat.
example: For example, a person who watches over a group of sheep in the countryside is called a shepherd.
